book.title: The Telegraph All New Cryptic Crosswords 4

clue.text: Area of unrest causing middle-eastern currency summits to be put back

indicators.note: only the central letter of the following word is kept, the rest discarded

parts.note: the middle letter of the seven-letter word
the rouble is the Russian unit of currency

indicators.note: putting something back turns it round, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: summits are tops

explanation.surface: A Middle Eastern money crisis, with currencies tumbling from their highs, sparks unrest in the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-eastern currency' reads as one phrase, a rial or dinar; split it, so 'middle' picks a letter of 'eastern' and the currency is a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouble spot is a place where conflict or disorder keeps breaking out, which is an area of unrest.

clue.text: The dumb fools got a lift from a stranger

definitions.text: got a lift from a stranger

indicators.note: fools here is a verb, to trick or mess about with, so these letters are tampered with

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Some silly people hitchhiked and climbed into a stranger's car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumb fools' looks like a noun phrase; 'fools' is a verb acting on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchhikers thumb a lift by holding out a thumb at passing cars, so thumbed means hitched a ride.

clue.text: Turn up with poor actor's script

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a turn is a go, as in 'your go'
a ham is an overacting, poor actor

explanation.surface: An actor shows up with a bad script for the play.
explanation.walkthrough: Ogham is the ancient alphabet of notches carved on standing stones in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogham is a writing system, an early Irish script of strokes along a line.

clue.text: Invoice on a good French source of Grenache — and still water!

parts.note: an invoice is a bill
taken as written
bon is French for good

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the first letter of the next word is used

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: A bill for some fine French red wine, with a glass of still water on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Grenache is a grape and wine, and still water sounds like the drink beside it; here it is a lake. A billabong is Australian for a stagnant backwater.
explanation.definitionFit: A billabong is a cut-off pool or backwater of an Australian river, water that does not flow.

clue.text: Worries about what consumer does

definitions.meaning: first meaning: troubles, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: Fretting over the behaviour of shoppers.
explanation.walkthrough: A consumer sounds like a shopper; here it is anyone who consumes food.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat at someone is to bother them, and a consumer of food eats it.

clue.text: Work of art to rip into pieces?

definitions.text: Work of art to rip into pieces?

indicators.note: torn into pieces, the letters fall apart and are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painting someone might want to tear up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer, a work of art one might rip up, while 'art to rip' supplies the letters; 'art' does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A portrait is a painting or drawing of a person, a classic work of art, and torn pieces are what ripping one leaves.

clue.text: Half-a-crown?

parts.note: surface reading: the old British coin worth two shillings and sixpence; setter's reading: a headpiece that is only part of a full crown

explanation.walkthrough: A half-crown was a pre-decimal British coin; read literally, the phrase describes a partial crown worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiara is a jewelled semicircular band worn on the front of the head, like a crown cut in half.

clue.text: Gambles, accepting request for containers

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: gambles are bets
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: A punter takes bets when asked about storage boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Baskets are woven receptacles for carrying things, so they are containers.

clue.text: Pestered communist to support symbol of office

indicators.note: in a down clue, what supports something sits beneath it, so this piece comes second

parts.note: a badge marks someone's rank or office
red is the colour of communism

explanation.surface: A left-wing official harassed into backing the mayor's chain of office.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to nag them persistently, which is what pestering is.

clue.text: Provide cover for winning gun emplacement

parts.note: a side that is winning is up, as in 'two up'
a holster is where a pistol is placed and carried

explanation.surface: Military orders to camouflage a successful artillery position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gun emplacement' suggests a fortified battery, but here it is just the leather case a handgun sits in.
explanation.definitionFit: To upholster furniture is to fit it with padding and a fabric covering, so it means to provide cover for it.

clue.text: A year has transformed maids abroad

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something transformed has been changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Y is the standard abbreviation for year
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spending a year overseas has changed some housemaids completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' looks like the verb of the sentence, but it is part of the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayahs are nursemaids or domestic servants in India and other former colonies, so they are maids found abroad.

clue.text: City lad accepting business degree

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
the Master of Business Administration

explanation.surface: A young man from the city taking a business qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City lad' reads as one phrase, a young man from town; the city alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombay is the former name of Mumbai, the large Indian port city.

clue.text: Integral part of a percussion instrument

indicators.note: to part something is to split it up, so the letters are broken and reassembled

parts.note: the eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Something essential to the make-up of a drum or cymbal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Integral part' reads as a stock phrase meaning essential component; split it, so 'part' works on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangle is a steel bar bent into three sides and struck with a beater, a standard orchestral percussion instrument.

clue.text: One very fierce doctor with endless pain

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
agony is intense pain

explanation.surface: A fearsome physician whose suffering never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is used of a fierce, intimidating person, typically a formidable older woman, so it names one very fierce.

clue.text: New role — get a new identity!

indicators.note: something made new is remade, so the following letters are rebuilt in another order

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor told to take on a fresh part and become someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New role' reads as a theatre part; 'New' works on the letters that follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: An alter ego is a second self or persona a person adopts, a new identity alongside their own.

clue.text: Course of study for a ref isn't difficult

indicators.note: difficult can mean awkward or troublesome, and these letters are made to misbehave and reshuffle

parts.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Training to become a football referee is said to be easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Difficult' looks like part of the claim about the course, but it is the signal to rearrange the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine arts, such as painting and sculpture, are a subject offered as a university degree course.

clue.text: Great elation about Britain's first plant

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: euphoria is intense happiness

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: Britain overjoyed at its first prize-winning flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphorbia is the genus of spurges, a large family of plants with milky sap, including the poinsettia.

clue.text: Honest about a hand at poker?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: five cards in sequence

explanation.surface: Is a card player telling the truth about the hand he holds?
explanation.definitionFit: Straight means truthful and upright, and in poker it names five consecutive cards of mixed suits.

clue.text: Sue fired one-in front of the door

parts.note: fired as in set alight
the Roman numeral for one
a gate stands in front of a house's door

explanation.surface: A woman called Sue sacked someone right on the doorstep.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue looks like a woman's name doing the firing; it is the verb meaning take to court, and 'fired' means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: To litigate is to take a dispute to court, which is what suing someone means.

clue.text: Allowed to drink when disappointed

parts.note: to let is to allow
to down a drink is to swallow it in one

explanation.surface: Someone permitted to have a drink when feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel let down is to be disappointed by someone failing you, so the phrase works as an adjective.

clue.text: Spinner's pride broken by first of sixes

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so these letters are reassembled in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler's self-esteem is shattered when batsmen keep hitting him for six.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a spinner is a slow bowler, and a six is the biggest hit; the spinner here is one that spins a web.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins silk to build its web, so it is literally a spinner.

clue.text: How much radiation in free nitrogen doesn't have one?

indicators.note: set free, the letters are released from their order and rearranged
lacking one means the letter standing for one is removed

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one, which is removed

explanation.surface: Asking how much radiation comes from nitrogen gas lacking a single atom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free nitrogen' sounds like chemistry, but 'free' is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The röntgen, also spelt roentgen, is an old unit measuring exposure to X-rays and gamma rays, so it states a quantity of radiation.

clue.text: Act firm to confront heartless activist traitor

indicators.note: to confront is to stand face to face, so these pieces are placed before the next one

parts.note: a turn is a performer's act on stage
Co. is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: with its heart gone, only the outside letters of the word remain

parts.note: the first and last letters only

explanation.surface: A company acts against a ruthless campaigner who betrayed it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Act' and 'firm' look like a verb and an adjective (act firmly); they are the nouns a stage act and a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who deserts one side for the other, which makes them a traitor.

clue.text: Ending changed to African country dance

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: the Congo is a country in central Africa

explanation.surface: Changing an ending to an African nation's traditional dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says only that the last letter changes; the dance the definition names tells you the new letter is A.
explanation.definitionFit: The conga is a Latin American dance performed in a long line, each dancer holding the one in front.

clue.text: Sphere of influence of party chief?

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
chief means main, principal

explanation.surface: Asking how far a political party leader's power reaches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party chief' suggests a political leader; it splits into a celebration and an adjective meaning principal.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is an area of territory or activity under someone's control, which is a sphere of influence.

clue.text: Legal defence of a former politician with ego

parts.note: taken as written
a Liberal, member of the old British Liberal Party
the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: An ex-MP's self-regarding case in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Party merged into the Liberal Democrats in 1988, so a Lib is a former kind of politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim that the accused was elsewhere when the crime happened, a standard legal defence.

clue.text: Show pleasure when involved in rising corruption

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read from bottom to top
involved in means wrapped up inside, so the letters sit within the word

parts.note: four consecutive letters inside the word

explanation.surface: Someone who is delighted to be mixed up in growing graft.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat purrs when contented, so to purr is to make a sound expressing pleasure.

clue.text: An instrument for gangsters to conceal

indicators.note: the words conceal something, holding it inside them across the gap

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A violin case for mobsters to hide their weapon in.
explanation.walkthrough: The instrument in the surface is a gangster's gun in a violin case; the answer is a musical one, and it sits inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ is a keyboard instrument sounded by pipes, found in churches and concert halls.

clue.text: George, finding out the truth, was complaining

definitions.note: a participle; the clue's past continuous verb phrase stands in for it

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for George, as in GR, George Rex
to rumble someone is to see through them and discover the truth

explanation.surface: George whinged once he discovered what had really happened.
explanation.walkthrough: To rumble is British slang for to find out or see through a deception.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling is muttering discontentedly, which is what someone who was complaining was doing.

clue.text: Argument over change and action being rescheduled

parts.note: to change is to alter

indicators.note: something rescheduled is put in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dispute breaks out over changes and a postponed lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: An altercation is a noisy quarrel or dispute, a synonym for an argument.
